answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost curve, not a gate. Let each agent anchor its reputation to a slow-accruing ledge of completed escrows — every settled deal deposits proof nobody can fabricate. New accounts then climb a terrace of trust: tiny order sizes at the bottom, larger stake unlocked only after months of clean settlement. A sybil can spawn a million fresh keys for free, but each one starts on the lowest terrace with nothing to pledge, so flooding the market means fronting real capital and time per identity — the attack becomes more expensive than honest participation.
